10. Next, Mr. Faiz, the learned Advocate, contends that the statement of the witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure particularly those of PWs 2, 3, 5, and 6 were recorded by the investigating officer at a very belated stage without any reasonable ground and in view of such delay in recording the statement of the PWs under section 161 CrPC, their evidence ought to have been taken with a grain of salt and not relied upon by the learned Sessions Judge in convicting the accused appellants. The learned Advocate also has made a grievance that the defence case has not been considered side by side with that of the prosecution by trial Court and as a result the defence has been seriously prejudiced. His further contention is that for non-production of some material charge-sheet witnesses the trial Court ought to have drawn adverse presumption against the prosecution case and given benefit of doubt to the accused. His last submission is that the sentence passed against the appellants is too severe in the facts and circumstances of the case and deserves reduction if at all the conviction is maintained by this Court. 

 22. Now, with regard to the submission of the learned Advocate for the appellants that as some material, charge-sheet witnesses have been withheld and hence the learned Sessions Judge ought to have drawn an adverse presumption against the prosecution case, it may be noticed that out of 17 charge-sheeted witnesses, 10 witnesses have been examined by the prosecution and out of the rest charge-sheet witness Nos. 15 and 16 are police men and charge-sheet witness Nos. 5 Mohammad AIi, 7 Alkas Ali, 9 Abdul Barek, AItaf AIi, Chairman, of course have not been produced in court as witnesses. But it is well-settled that the prosecution is not bound to examine all the cited witnesses to prove its case. Even if one prosecution witness is fully reliable and trustworthy, then conviction of an accused can be based upon such evidence. It will, however, depend upon the facts and circumstances of each case. In the instant case PWs 1-6 are said to be the eye-witnesses of the occurrence and so far the other charge-sheet witnesses namely Mohammad Ali, Alkas Ali, Abdur Barek are concerned they were cited as witnesses but subsequently it transpired that they were unwilling to depose in favour of the prosecution being influenced, by the accused. It appears from the record of the case that an application on behalf of the prosecution was filed before the learned Sessions Judge seeking exemption from examining those witnesses and the prayer was allowed by him by an order dated 17.9.1986. 

 23. Thus we find good reasons for non-production of the said witnesses, Therefore, the question of drawing adverse presumption against the prosecution case for non-production of the alleged charge-sheet witnesses does not arise at all in this case.
